headline: Load-shedding worsens in 21 southwestern districts, deficit hits 116MW
summary: The power deficit in these areas has reached 116MW, leading to increased outages and significant disruption for residents and businesses.
details: Load-shedding has significantly worsened across 21 southwestern districts of Bangladesh. The region is currently experiencing a power deficit of 116 megawatts.
This increased deficit has led to more frequent and prolonged power outages in these areas. Residents and businesses in the affected districts are directly impacted by the worsening situation.

The 21 southwestern districts are facing considerable challenges due to the unreliable electricity supply. The extent of the deficit indicates a substantial gap between power generation and demand in the region.

The ongoing power crisis underscores the need for effective energy management strategies. The situation continues to pose difficulties for daily activities and economic operations across the affected areas.

headline: 1,702 candidates appointed through 45th BCS final gazette
summary: The Public Administration Ministry has published the final gazette for the 45th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examination, appointing 1,702 candidates to various cadres.
details: The Public Administration Ministry has published the final gazette for the 45th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examination. This gazette confirms the appointment of 1,702 candidates to various government cadres.

Issued on Wednesday night, the gazette instructs these newly appointed officials to report to their designated offices by November 1. Their respective cadre-controlling ministries or divisions will assign their specific roles.
caption:
Over 1,700 candidates have been appointed through the 45th BCS final gazette!

The Public Administration Ministry has published the final gazette for the 45th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examination. This gazette confirms the appointment of 1,702 candidates to various government cadres.

Issued on Wednesday night, the gazette instructs these newly appointed officials to report to their designated offices by November 1. Their respective cadre-controlling ministries or divisions will assign their specific roles.
